records.title: ACRFence: Preventing Semantic Rollback Attacks in Agent Checkpoint-Restore
records.relevance_note: Concrete checkpoint-restore failure model plus restore-path mitigation.
records.reason_included: Measured rollback-induced duplicate side effects and proposed a tool-boundary guard.

claim_snippets.claim_text: In the authors' testbed, all 10 checkpoint-restore trials produced duplicate commits, while a no-checkpoint baseline produced none.
Token-reuse attacks on rolled-back authorization state succeeded under stateless validation and were rejected under stateful validation.
ACRFence mitigates restore-time re-execution by logging irreversible tool effects and enforcing replay-or-fork semantics after semantic comparison of the post-restore call.

records.title: Security: Unsafe pickle deserialization in state restoration (CWE-502)
records.exception_reason: Filed just outside the primary window and retained for a concrete unsafe state-restoration failure in OpenHands.
records.relevance_note: State restore path with explicit unsafe deserialization details.
records.reason_included: Concrete restoration code path, attack surface, and safer replacement options.

claim_snippets.claim_text: State and metrics are restored with pickle.loads without integrity verification or restricted deserialization.
A crafted state file delivered through S3, GCS, or webhook-backed stores could trigger code execution during restore.
Suggested fixes include JSON or dataclass-based serialization, RestrictedUnpickler, or signing serialized state with HMAC.

claim_snippets.claim_text: Rewind nullifies session-scoped auth or tenant context injected during create_session, breaking subsequent invocations after recovery.
A reported workaround is a custom rewind implementation that preserves a blocklist of protected session keys.
Reinjecting state after every rewind introduces a race window, and existing app:/user: prefixes do not cover all protected-key needs.
